info.description:
# pylogix - A Python Package for Rockwell Automation ControlLogix, CompactLogix and Micro8xx PLC's

Pylogix is a Python package developed by  [Pylogix](https://pylogix.com/) ,  -  [https://pylogix.com/](https://pylogix.com/), which is a software company that allows you to easily read/write values from tags in Rockwell Automation ControlLogix, CompactLogix, and Micro8xx PLC's over Ethernet I/P.

## Features

-   Pylogix only supports PLC's that are programmed with RSLogix5000/Studio5000 or Connected Components Workbench (Micro8xx), and models like PLC5, SLC, MicroLogix are  _not_  supported as they use a different protocol.
    
-   Pylogix can discover many devices that support CIP objects that allow for automatic discovery (like RSLinx does), but will likely not be able to interact with them in any other meaningful way, as it is intended to talk to the above mentioned PLC's and is only tested against them.
    
-   For general support or questions, Pylogix has a discord channel.
    

## Getting Started

To install pylogix using pip, use the following command:

Copy`pip install pylogix` 

To install a previous version before major changes, use:

Copy`pip install pylogix==0.3.7` 

To upgrade to the latest version:

Copy`pip install pylogix --upgrade` 

Alternatively, to clone the repo and manually install it:

Copy`git clone https://github.com/dmroeder/pylogix.git
cd pylogix
python setup.py install --user` 

To verify the pylogix installation, try:

Copy`python3
import pylogix
pylogix.__version__` 

## Usage

Pylogix has features beyond simply reading/writing, and you should refer to the documentation for more information. Still, we present an example of how to read a tag and print out its value:

Copy`from pylogix import PLC

with PLC() as comm:
    comm.IPAddress = '192.168.1.9'
    ret = comm.Read('MyTagName')
    print(ret.TagName, ret.Value, ret.Status)` 

If your PLC is in a slot other than zero (like can be done with ControlLogix), you can specify the slot with:

Copy`comm.ProcessorSlot = 2` 

If you are working with a Micro8xx PLC, you must set the Micro800 flag since the path is different:

Copy`comm.Micro800 = True` 

It is also possible to set a specific maximum size for requests/replies. If not specified, the package will try a Large, then a Small Forward Open (for Implicit, "Connected" sessions):

Copy`comm.ConnectionSize = 508`
